title: Lightning SDK onramp: rollout contracts + sample flows (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience

This is a compact, hands-on draft for quickly onboarding internal teams (platform, product, and integrators) to the Redwood SDKs with an emphasis on safe rollouts and clear prompt/output contracts. The goal is a 20–45 minute guided experience that leaves an engineer with:
  - a working local dev loop (CLI + local server),
  - a simple client example that calls Redwood (hosted/dedicated),
  - a rollout plan that includes canary checks and prompt-contract tests, and
  - a minimal set of artifacts (prompts, tests, telemetry checks) they can copy into their repo.

High-level constraints / principles
  - Keep friction minimal for engineers who already use CLI tooling and monorepos.
  - Provide explicit, copy-pasteable contract tests (not just guidelines).
  - Make rollback trivial: feature flag + fallback model route + circuit breaker.
  - Surface cost and latency tradeoffs up-front so PMs can weigh decisions during the demo.

What success looks like\  
  - Developer can run the quickstart and see a deterministic response from a pinned model variant in < 20 minutes.
  - Canary rollout detects a regresssion in model output for a curated prompt set within 1 hour of traffic.
  - A minimal telemetry dashboard shows per-prompt latency and token cost for the canary users.

Quickstart flow (20–45 min)\
 1) Prereqs (2–3 min)\    - Node 18 / Python 3.10, Docker optional\    - Access token / team API key (instructions to request in README)
 2) Bootstrap (5 min)\    - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/lightning-onramp.git\    - cd lightning-onramp && ./bin/setup.sh (this script: installs deps, creates .env.example -> .env, sets REDWOOD_API_KEY env var placeholder)
 3) Local shim server (5 min)\    - npm run dev (or python -m lightning.local)\    - server exposes /generate and proxies to Redwood SDK with an in-memory cache for prefix reuse\    - developer can toggle environment to point to hosted vs dedicated via .env
 4) Minimal client example (5 min)\    - src/examples/quickreply.js demonstrates: initialize client, set model: redwood/gpt-small:2025-06-15, stream responses, handle tool-calls (JSON)
 5) Prompt contract tests (10 min)\    - tests/prompt-contracts.yml contains 6 seed prompts with expected structured output assertions (exact match for some keys, regex for free-text fields)\    - run: yarn test:contract (or pytest tests/test_prompt_contracts.py)\    - failing tests show diffs and a suggest command to pin model/temperature or add a post-processing filter
 6) Canary rollout sample (5–10 min)\    - sample infra: feature-flag gate (LaunchDarkly or local flag) + route rule that sends 5% traffic to model variant v2 and 95% to stable v1\    - script: infra/deploy-canary.sh creates the route and a lightweight synthetic runner that replays the prompt contract set at 1req/min/user for 60 minutes\    - expected outputs: canary telemetry dashboard, contract pass/fail rate, latency and token-cost histogram

Rolling it into your app (recommended checklist)\
  - Add prompt-contracts.yml to repo root (one canonical place for test prompts)\  - Wire up pre-deploy hook: run contract tests against the pinned model (fast local runner)\  - Add an automated canary runner job in CI that executes after deploy and signals SLOs (contract pass-rate > 95%, 95p latency < 1s)\  - Implement fallback: if canary fails > threshold, flip traffic back and open alert (PagerDuty)\  - Instrument telemetry: per-route token cost, per-prompt latency, error rate, and hallucination indicator (heuristic)

Prompt contracts: minimal sample format\
  - YAML-based, human-editable, single file for the quickstart (examples in tests/)\  - Fields: id, description, prompt_template, expected_schema, exact_assertions, regex_assertions, tolerance_notes\  - Example entry (text form):
    - id: invoice-summarize-01
      description: "extract total, date, vendor from small invoice text"
      prompt_template: "Summarize the invoice:\n{{invoice_text}}"
      expected_schema: "{total: string, date: string, vendor: string}"
      exact_assertions: ["vendor == 'ACME Corp'"]
      regex_assertions: ["total: \$\d+\.\d{2}"]

Safety + rollout gating checks (practical)\
  - Contract pass rate: reject canary if > 2 contract failures in a sliding 100-sample window\  - Semantic drift: compute embedding-distance from golden responses; alert if average cosine distance > 0.18\  - Latency SLO: 95th percentile must be < target for the route (configurable per product)\  - Cost guardrail: if per-request token cost increases > 50% vs baseline for canary, fail and rollback

Telemetry and observability (minimum viable)\
  - Lightweight dashboard widgets: canary pass/fail, contract failure examples (with diffs), token cost trending, 95p latency, embedding-drift chart\  - Eventing: contract_fail events include prompt_id, input, expected, actual, request_id, model_variant\  - Quick debugging flow: developer clicks failing sample -> launches local replay -> iterates prompt or pins model

Developer ergonomics notes (lessons learned from internal pilots)\
  - Keep the local runner deterministic by pinning seed and model version in examples. Randomized temperature should be off by default for contract tests.\  - Provide pre-baked prompt templates for common patterns (extraction, summarization, classification) so teams can adapt quickly.\  - Include a tiny post-processing validator recipe for JSON outputs to reduce false negatives in tests.

Open items / TODOs\
  - Finalize the prompt-contract spec (add canonical JSON Schema mapping) [owner: Rina]\  - Add a lightweight LaunchDarkly-free feature flag shim for teams without LD access [owner: Owen]\  - Add an example for the Private deployment flow (VPC/KMS) and how to run contract tests against an on-prem instance [owner: Diego]\  - Decide on the telemetry sink (Options: Grafana + Prometheus vs. hosted Redwood Console integration). Quick preference poll: Redwood Console (integrated) -> +1, Grafana -> -1

Appendix: helpful commands (copy-paste)\
  - clone + setup: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/lightning-onramp.git && cd lightning-onramp && ./bin/setup.sh\  - run local server: npm run dev\  - run contract tests: yarn test:contract\  - deploy canary: infra/deploy-canary.sh --percent 5 --duration 60m\
Notes to self: keep this intentionally compact. Next pass: add screenshots of the quick dashboard, add a one-page cheat sheet for PMs explaining the tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality).
